finding.claim: OS command injection: the unauthenticated /ping endpoint concatenates the user-supplied `host` query parameter into a shell command string passed to exec(), so shell metacharacters give remote command execution.
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which runs through a shell

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping with no auth middleware
req.query.host is concatenated into the command string and passed to exec(), which spawns /bin/sh -c
Command stdout is returned to the caller, so output is exfiltrated directly

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allow-list, or escaping. No authentication or authorization middleware. exec is used rather than execFile with an argument array. The only other code is app.listen(3001), and there is no reverse proxy or filter in the repo. The query value can also be an array or object (e.g. host[]=a), which stringifies but does not block injection. Example payload: /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id or $(id).

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) in an unauthenticated route (tools.js:6) with no validation, escaping or middleware, and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so `;id` yields output; tools.js is the only file in the repo.

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) with no auth, validation or escaping in the handler at tools.js:6, and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so `127.0.0.1;id` gives unauthenticated RCE with output returned.
